assertion.rationale: F7: anything executing inside a verify job — a compromised action, a malicious transitive dependency pulled by npm ci, a tampered audit script — can read the job-scoped ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL/TOKEN, mint a token with subject environment:demo, and exchange it against the Owner-capable deployer in three HTTP calls, going Reader to Owner. Nothing prevents this non-privileged execution context from invoking the privileged function, and (compounded by F9's absent diagnostic logging) the escalation is not captured in any audit log.

recommendation: Federate a distinct verify environment to mls-verifier with deployment-branch policy restricting both demo and verify to main; assert the distinctness of the verify subject from the deployer's in verify-g0.ps1. Combined with F9's fix, capture the resulting OIDC token exchanges in diagnostic logging so any future privileged-function execution is auditable.
